newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS BACK TO BASICS NOW BUDGET OUT OF WAY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS BACK TO BASICS NOW BUDGET OUT OF WAY.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) were seen focusing sharply again on international data now the fallout from the 1997 budget was out of the way, dealers said.
Domestic news -- such as the release of September unemployment on Thursday -- would have little impact, they said.
"The main figure we have is on Friday with the U.S. (September) payrolls," one trader said.

Most dealers did not expect a meeting of Belgian public sector unions on the budget on Friday to lead to any kind of concerted strike action, despite a call last week from one union for a mass protest before the end of the month.
"The budget will not really hurt any one particular group in any particular way," one trader commented.

"The government has all the power in their hands," another said, referring to the "special powers" the government was voted to push through the budget by decree. "They can strike as much as they want but there won't be anything changed."

Optimism over the budget and an overnight rally in U.S. Treasuries on a soft purchasing managers index helped push the yield on 10-year OLOs down to 6.15 percent on Wednesday from 6.19 percent at Tuesday's close. The spread over equivalent Bunds narrowed to a record 12 basis points from 13.

Dealers said they expected the spread to narrow further to around 10 basis points in the coming days, especially if Bunds trade down: OLOs traditionally lag Bunds and tend to outperform in down moves.
The market remained well supported on Wednesday thanks to a large U.S. bank buying, one trader said.
U.S. September non-farm payrolls are forecast to have risen by 175,000 compared with 250,000 in August. Unemployment is seen at 5.2 percent from 5.1.
